slm.label: Small Language Model (SLM)
slm.definition: A language model small enough to run on commodity hardware — phones, laptops, single GPUs — and to be fine-tuned on a single institution's data. Typically under ~10B parameters today, but the boundary is defined by deployability, not size.

frontier-model.label: Frontier model
frontier-model.definition: The largest, most capable models trained at any given moment, typically by a small number of well-funded labs. Often general-purpose, often closed, and rarely deployable outside vendor infrastructure.

lwdr.label: LWD-R
lwdr.definition: The four layers of openness in the accord: Logic, Weights, Data, and Representation. Each layer is independently disclosable; openness is the composition of what is open across all four.

tokenizer.label: Tokenizer
tokenizer.definition: The component that breaks text into the discrete units a model operates on. A tokenizer trained primarily on English fragments other languages into many more tokens, raising cost and degrading quality. Tokenizer openness is part of language coverage.

fine-tuning.label: Fine-tuning
fine-tuning.definition: Continuing training of an existing model on new data, typically narrower or more specialized than the original training set. Fine-tuning lets institutions adapt a model to their domain without redoing pretraining.

distillation.label: Distillation
distillation.definition: Training a smaller model to imitate a larger one's outputs, often using synthetic data generated by the larger model. Provenance carries through: a distilled model inherits the lineage of its teacher.

quantization.label: Quantization
quantization.definition: Reducing the numerical precision of a model's weights (e.g., from 16-bit to 4-bit) to make it smaller and faster. Quantization is a deployment-time transformation that changes the operative model; it must be documented for reproducibility.

moe.label: Mixture of Experts (MoE)
moe.definition: An architecture where many smaller specialist sub-networks (experts) are combined via a learned routing network. The router is part of Logic; the experts are Weights. Reproducibility requires both.

inference.label: Inference
inference.definition: Running a trained model on input to produce output, as opposed to training the model. Local inference means inference on hardware controlled by the deploying institution rather than vendor APIs.

osaid.label: Open Source AI Definition (OSAID)
osaid.definition: The Open Source Initiative's definition of an open-source AI system, requiring access to code, parameters, and information about training data sufficient for someone other than the original developer to reproduce, study, and modify the system.
